claim.title: Colorado/Denver local-information neuron
claim.lede: This neuron tracks Colorado and Denver locality. Across a billion tokens its product is strongly positively selective for “ Denver,” “ Colorado,” “Colorado,” “Denver,” and “ Boulder,” and its +1-product logit projection promotes those place tokens. Its largest positive spikes occur where Colorado-linked text reaches a local address, venue, listing, or phone number, suggesting the neuron carries place-specific local information rather than merely reacting to the word Colorado.
claim.one_paragraph: Positive product is sparse but highly peaked: the mean is 0.005, median -0.096, p99.9 is 22.75, p99.99 is 134, and the maximum is 364, while only 6.2% of gates are positive. At the maximum, gate 20.25 and value 18.0 jointly open. The top 0.01% product cases are overwhelmingly Colorado contexts—Denver Post politics, the Colorado Avalanche, a Boulder film festival, Front Range weather, and Denver-area contacts—and positive peaks often land at “at,” spaces, or punctuation before 303/720/970 phone numbers or local listing digits. Token selectivity is the strongest evidence: at 10% of the +364 extreme, “ Denver” hits 87.1% of 14,277 occurrences (mean product 93.5), “ Colorado” 84.0%, “Denver” 80.6%, “Colorado” 79.5%, and “ Boulder” 74.3%. Output projection at +1 product boosts “ Boulder” (+0.743), “ Colorado” (+0.729), and “ Denver” (+0.722). The limitation is that activation peaks mix place semantics with local number formatting; ablation effects are context-specific, so telephone/address retrieval is a plausible response mode, not a proven separate function.
claim.negative_pole: The negative side is much weaker and lacks a clean opposite concept. The corpus minimum is -55.25, where gate is still positive at 9.94 but value turns negative at -5.56; extreme negative cases sit at phone-number, listing, coordinate, or record-number boundaries from non-Colorado local pages, including Utah and North Dakota material. Token selectivity beyond the -5.53 threshold is modest: “RING” 31.6%, “ BYU” 15.5%, “ Dakota” 14.2%, and “ Fargo” 11.1%, with mean products only around -0.9 to -3.3. Thus negative product appears to encode suppression in off-region local-number and official-record contexts rather than an anti-Colorado feature.
claim.what_would_change_my_mind: Strong positive selectivity and the logit-lens promotion agree, but if Denver or Colorado occurrences usually produced near-zero product after controlling for sentence position, or if a matched phone-number probe drove the same activation without any place context, I would abandon the locality interpretation and call this a local-contact or formatting neuron.
